chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me of it, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked about a man who is in his salat (prayer), and a pumpkin seed comes out of him—what should he do? He said: If it came out clean from feces, then nothing is upon him, and it has not invalidated his wudu (ablution). But if it came out smeared with feces, then he must repeat the wudu (ablution); and if he is in his salat (prayer), he should break the salat (prayer), and repeat the wudu (ablution) and the salat (prayer).

key_terms.الْعَذِرَةِ: feces, the impurity determining the ruling
key_terms.حَبُّ الْقَرْعِ: a pumpkin seed; here, a small expelled object used as the legal example
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being performed
key_terms.قَطَعَ الصَّلَاةَ: he should break the salat (prayer), i.e., discontinue it due to invalidation
key_terms.مُتَلَطِّخًا: smeared or soiled, meaning contaminated with impurity
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُ: his wudu (ablution), the state of ritual purity in question

ai.seo_question: Does something exiting the body during salat (prayer) invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding ritual purity during salat (prayer) when a small object exits the body. If it emerges clean of feces, the wudu (ablution) remains valid; if it is contaminated with feces, wudu (ablution) must be repeated, and the salat (prayer) must also be restarted if one is already praying.
